---
title: "Installation"
description: "Install conformalforecast, verify it imports, and pick the optional extras you need."
---

## From PyPI

```bash
pip install conformalforecast
```

Or with uv:

```bash
uv add conformalforecast
```

The core install is pure Python and depends only on `numpy`, `pandas` and
`scipy`. Python 3.10 or newer is required.

## Verify the install

```bash
python -c "import conformalforecast; print(conformalforecast.__version__)"
```

## Optional extras

Everything beyond the calibration math is an extra, so the base install never
pulls a forecasting framework:

| Extra | Installs | Needed for |
|---|---|---|
| `nixtla` | statsforecast, mlforecast, neuralforecast | the Nixtla adapters |
| `spci` | quantile-forest | `SequentialPredictiveConformalInference` |
| `plotting` | matplotlib | plotting helpers |
| `all` | all of the above | — |

```bash
pip install "conformalforecast[nixtla]"
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Importing the package never imports a forecasting library

The Nixtla adapters are re-exported lazily, so `import conformalforecast` does
not import statsforecast, mlforecast, neuralforecast or torch. The library is
imported the first time you touch the adapter that needs it, and if the extra is
missing you get an `ImportError` naming the exact `pip install` command.
:::

`CallableAdapter` needs no extra at all — it wraps any function and is pure
numpy, which makes it the quickest way to try the package against a model you
already have.

## From a git checkout

For development, clone the repository and use the `devenv` target, which syncs
every extra plus the dev group and installs the pre-commit hooks:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Nixtla/conformalforecast.git
cd conformalforecast
make devenv
```

See [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/Nixtla/conformalforecast/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for the test, lint and documentation workflow.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Alpha versioning

`conformalforecast` is in early development and the API is unstable until
v0.2.0. Pin a version if you depend on exact interval values.
:::
